gen.title: Building a numeric history from atoms and fossils
gen.orderNote: Steps follow the order described in the text.

steps.label: Minerals contain radioactive elements for dating
steps.quote: Now we can use minerals that contain naturally occurring radioactive elements to calculate the numeric age of a rock in years.

steps.label: Parent atoms change to daughter at constant rate
steps.quote: The change from parent to daughter happens at a constant rate, called the half-life.

steps.label: Half-life sets time for half to decay
steps.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.

steps.label: Laboratory counts parent and daughter atoms
steps.quote: Precise laboratory measurements of the number of remaining atoms of the parent and the number of atoms of the new daughter produced are used

steps.label: Isotopic methods date mineral formation
steps.quote: Isotopic techniques are used to measure the time at which a particular mineral within a rock was formed.

steps.label: Datable rock paired with fossil relative age
steps.quote: a rock that can be dated isotopically is found together with rocks that can be assigned relative ages because of their fossils.

steps.label: Many samples studied to assign boundary age
steps.quote: Many samples, usually from several different places, must be studied before assigning a numeric age to a boundary on the geologic time scale.
